pick.why: First-party and maintained with Claude Code; run it in a dedicated Chrome profile so agent actions stay away from personal accounts

best_free.name: Chrome DevTools MCP with --autoConnect (Google)
best_free.what: Google's official MCP server that attaches to your running Chrome (M144+) after an Allow prompt, so the agent works in your logged-in profile
best_free.why: Free, Apache-2.0, maintained by the Chrome DevTools team, ~54k stars; uses the browser you already keep updated instead of a separate Chromium fork
best_free.free_limits: n/a; needs Node.js LTS and Chrome M144+; enable chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging and approve the connection dialog
best_free.maintained: active; release tags not shown on repo page
best_free.install: claude mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --autoConnect  (or /plugin marketplace add ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp; /plugin install chrome-devtools-mcp@chrome-devtools-plugins)

decision: Claude in Chrome is first-party and needs no extra browser. The best free route is Chrome DevTools MCP with --autoConnect, which drives your normal logged-in Chrome after you approve each connection; give it a dedicated Chrome profile if you do not want the agent near sensitive sessions. Choose BrowserOS neo only if you want a wholly separate agent browser binary and accept AGPL and a smaller project.
details: BrowserOS neo moved to candidates: AGPL-3.0 Chromium fork, ~14.2k stars, Linux x64 only for neo, anonymous usage events on by default.
